alternate_names: Shree Sant Gnyananeshwar Maharaj Samadhi Mandir

history.summary: Samadhi shrine of Sant Dnyaneshwar (1275–1296), the 13th-century Marathi saint, poet, and philosopher of the Varkari tradition, author of the Dnyaneshwari (Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita) and Amrutanubhav. He took sanjeevan samadhi — voluntary live entombment in a meditative state — at age 21 in 1296; the temple (built 1570) stands over the underground chamber on the banks of the Indrayani River. Devotees revere him as an avatar of Lord Krishna. Alandi is the starting point of the annual Sant Dnyaneshwar Palkhi procession to Pandharpur.

name: Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj Samadhi Mandir
town_description: Alandi is a pilgrimage town in Khed taluka of Pune district, Maharashtra, on the banks of the Indrayani River about 19–22 km northeast of Pune. It is best known as the place where Sant Dnyaneshwar took sanjeevan samadhi in 1296. Besides the samadhi mandir, the town has the Vitthal-Rakhumai, Ram, Krishna, and Muktai temples, and is the starting point of the annual Dnyaneshwar Palkhi procession to Pandharpur.

travel.railway: Pune Junction (~25 km) (verify); a local Alandi Railway Station is listed ~0.6 km away (verify)
travel.road: Buses run from Swargate Bus Station, Pune to Alandi; taxis/private cabs easily available from Pune

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ashadh (June–July) and Kartik (November–December) for the Palkhi season (expect large crowds)
